«يا لعمق غنى حكمةِ اللهِ ومعرفته! ما أصعب أن تُستقصى أحكامه، وما أعجز أن تُدرك طرقه! فمن عرف ذهنَ الربِّ؟ أو من كان مستشارَه؟ أو من أعطاه أولاً فيُردّ إليه؟ لأنه منه وبواسطته وإليه كلّ شيء: له المجد إلى الأبد. آمين» (روم. 11:33–36).

يا لها من هتافٍ مفعمٍ بالحياة والتعبير كتبَه الرسول بولس! ونحن نعود اليوم لننظر في ترنيمة جديدة وكاتب ترنيمات جديد أيضاً، فلتكن عقولنا يقظة وقلوبنا منفتحة لنرى عمل يدِ الله.

وُلد ماثيو بريدجز في مالدن بمقاطعة إسيكس في إنجلترا في 14 يوليو 1800. بدأ ينشر الأبيات في عام 1825 واستمر حتى أصدر مجلدين صغيرين من الترانيم—Hymns of the Heart (1848) وThe Passion of Jesus (1852). من هنا سأتابع القصة بإعطاء نبذة موجزة عن حياة كاتب الترانيم في الكنيسة.

كان كاتب الترانيم الذي ندرسه في هذه المقالة جزءًا من كنيسة إنجلترا الأنجليكانية. حوالي منتصف القرن التاسع عشر، أصبح غير راضٍ عن الجماعة الكنسية التي كان معها ووجد نفسه يتبع قيادة جون هنري نيومان فيما سُمّي حركة أكسفورد. وفقًا للعالم في تاريخ الترانيم ألبرت بيلي، كانت هذه الحركة تتركز على «المطالبة لكنيستهم الأنجليكانية بالنسب الخطّي من الكنيسة الرسوليّة الأصلية.» سعياً وراء هذا، درس أتباع المنظمة التاريخ القديم للكنيسة وعقيدتها وخاصة طقوسها. وفي ذلك اكتشفوا ثروة من الترميمات اليونانية واللاتينية من أوائل قرون الكنيسة المسيحية.

كما أنّنا للأسف نرى جماعاتٍ عديدة في الكنيسة المسيحية اليوم، كذلك كان نطاق الأمور في منتصف القرن التاسع عشر. بدا أنّ حركة أكسفورد في بعض النواحي كانت منافسة بين الأسلوب القديم والجديد في ممارسة الأمور. في حالة الشخصية في قصتنا اليوم، يبدو أنّه رأى مسارًا أكثر استقرارًا في الحفاظ على تقاليد الكنيسة الأم القديمة، ومع ذلك بدا أيضًا أن له إيمانًا حقيقيًا وحياً بربّنا ومخلّصنا يسوع المسيح. أود أن أضيف هنا أني أثق أن قراره اتُّخذ بضميرٍ صالحٍ تجاه الله، رغم أننا ننظر اليوم من منظور الألمانتيابيستي ونتساءل عن دوافعه للقيام بذلك.

سنستمر في قصتنا هنا. تحول ماثيو بريدجز إلى الكاثوليكية الرومانية، ورغبةً منه في المشاركة في التقاليد الغنية للترانيم في الكنيسة البروتستانتية، بدأ بكتابة ترانيم أصلية. تُميّز ترانيم السيد بريدجز بالروحانية والقوة الحقيقية. إحدى ترانيمه التي نُحبّها ونستمتع بها هي «قم أيها الغالب المجيد» (Rise, Glorious Conqueror). وبلا شك، أعظم ترنيمة له هي «تاجّوه بتيجانٍ كثيرة» (Crown Him with Many Crowns). ظهرت هذه الترانيمة لأول مرة في كتابه The Passion of Jesus، وقد أُعطيت في الأصل عنوان «ترنيمة السرافيم».

هناك خلفيةٌ مثيرة مرتبطة بهذه الترنيمة، بما في ذلك كيف أصبح لها 12 مقطعًا. ومن المفهوم أن جزءًا فقط من هذه المقاطع يُغنّى اليوم. يعتمد اختيار المقاطع على كتاب الترانيم.

كتب ماثيو بريدجز الأغنية في الأصل عام 1851. كتب ستة مقاطع، كلها مستندة إلى رؤيا 19:12: «... وعلى رأسه تيجان كثيرة.» استمر إصدار بريدجز حتى السبعينيات من ذلك القرن عندما ظهر رجل دين أنجليكاني تقي يُدعى غودفري ثرينج. كان غودفري قلقًا من أن هذه الترنيمة الشعبية تسمح بنشيد لاهوتٍ كاثوليكي داخل جماعاتٍ بروتستانتية. تمركزت مخاوفه ربما حول المقطع الثاني الأصلي لبريدجز، حيث أشار إلى السيدة العذراء المباركة. على ضوء ذلك، كتب ثرينج ستة مقاطع جديدة ونشرها في كتابه Hymns and Sacred Lyrics عام 1874.

لقد اختلطت المقاطع الاثني عشر وتبادلت عبر السنين. ومن المثير للاهتمام أن الثلاثة من بين ستة المقاطع الأكثر شيوعًا في كتب الترانيم اليوم كانت من تأليف بريدجز، وثلاثة كتبها ثرينج. الترنيمة، كما نُشرت في كتاب Hymns of the Church، تحذف تمامًا المقطع الثاني الأصلي وتستخدم المقاطع 1 و3 و4 وجزءًا من 5 وجزءًا من 6 من مقاطع بريدجز الأصلية الستة. المقاطع التي نغنيها في ذلك الكتاب مميزة في اختيار المقاطع أدناه. وأُدرجت أيضًا الستة الأبيات المزدوجة لثرينج.

تاجّوه بتيجانٍ كثيرة

—بريدجز

تاجّوه بتيجانٍ كثيرة، الحمل على عرشه؛
اسمعْ! كيف تُخمد الترانيم السماوية كل نغمٍ سوى نغمها؛
انهضي يا نفسي واغني له الذي مات لأجلك،
واسجد له ملكًا لا مثيل له مدى الدهر.

تاجّوه ابن العذراء! الإله المتجسّد المولود—
ذاك الذراع الذي نال بتلابيب القرمزية الدلالات التي تزيّن الآن جبينه!
ثمرة الوردة السرّية وكأصل تلك الوردة:
الجذر الذي منه يتدفّق الرحمة دائمًا—طفل بيت لحم!

تاجّوه ربّ السلام! الذي يَمسك سلطانه بصولجانٍ،
من قطبٍ إلى قطبٍ لتنتهي الحروب، مستغرقةً في الصلاة والتسبيح؛
لن يعرف ملكُه انقضاء، وحول قدميه المثقوبتين
تمتد زهور الفردوس معطّرةً بعطرٍ أبدي.

تاجّوه ربّ المحبة! انظرْ يدايه وجنبه—
جروحٌ غنية، ومع ذلك ظاهرةٌ في العلاء، مُمَجَّدة بالجمال؛
لا ملاك في السماء يقدر أن يتحمّل رؤيةً كهذه تمامًا،
بل ينحني بعينٍ مُحْتَرِقة أمام أسرارٍ لامعةٍ كهذه!

تاجّوه ربّ الدهور! السلطان على الزمن—
خالقُ الكرات الدوّارة، ببساطةٍ تفوق الوصف!
منعكسًا في بحرٍ من نورٍ حيث أمواجٌ أبدية
تعكس عرشه—اللانِهائي! الذي يَحيا—ويحب—ويخلّص.

تاجّوه ربّ السموات! واحدٌ معروفٌ مع الآب،
ومع الروح المباركة، المعطاة به منه من عرش الثالوث هناك!
هلمّوا! يا مخلّص—هلمّوا! لأنك متّ من أجلي؛
لا يَفشل ثناؤُك أبداً، أبدًا، عبر الأبدية!

تاجّوه بتيجانٍ كثيرة

—ثيرينج

تاجّوه بتيجانٍ من ذهب، يا أممًا كبارًا وصغارًا،
تاجّوه أيها الشهداء من القدم، الحملُ الذي ذُبِح ذاتَ يومٍ لأجل الجميع؛
الحملُ الذي ذُبِح لأجلهم الذين يأتون الآن بحمدهم،
كجواهر لتاجٍ يحيط بجبينه المقدّس.

تاجّوه ابنَ الله قبل أن تبدأ العوالم،
وأنتم الذين تطأون حيث وطأ، تاجّوه ابنَ الإنسان؛
هو الذي عرف كلّ حزنٍ يَقلِق الصدر البشري،
ويأخذه ويحمله لنفسه، لكي يستريح الجميع فيه.

تاجّوه ربّ النور، الذي على عالمٍ معتمٍ
في أزياء مجدٍ لا نهاية لها نشر رايته النّارية.
ورفَعها مرفوعةً عالياً، في السماء—في الأرض—تحتها،
لتكون علامة النصر على الشيطان والخطيئة والموت.

تاجّوه ربّ الحياة الذي انتصر على القبر،
وقام منتصرًا في الصراع من أجل الذين جاء ليخلّصهم؛
نرنّم الآن بمجدهِ، الذي مات وقام إلى العلاء.
الذي مات ليأتي بالحياة الأبدية ويحيى حتى يموت الموت.

تاجّوه ربّ الربّ الذي على كلّ شيء يملكُ السيادة،
الذي كان ذات يوم على الأرض، الكلمة المتجسِّدة، قُتل لفداء الخاطئين،
والآن يعيش في ممالك النور حيث القدّيسون مع الملائكة يغنون
ترانيمهم أمامه ليلًا ونهارًا، إلههم، مخلّصهم، ملكُهم.

تاجّوه ربّ السموات، متوّجًا في عوالمٍ فوقَ؛
تاجّوه الملكَ الذي أعطي له الاسم العجيب «المحبة»،
تاجّوه بتيجانٍ كثيرة، كما تَسقط العروش أمامه.
تاجّوه أيها الملوك بتيجانٍ كثيرة، لأنه هو ملك الجميع.

قضى ماثيو بريدجز سنواته الأخيرة في مقاطعة كيبك، كندا، ثم عاد إلى إنجلترا قبل وفاته في الأرض في 6 أكتوبر 1894 عن عمرٍ ناهز 94 عامًا. وعلى الرغم من أننا لا نجد تفاصيل كثيرة عن حياته، فقد ترك بين أيدينا واحدةً من أعظم الترانيم اليوم.

جزء كبير من دوام هذه الأغنية يعود إلى اللحن الذي تُقرَن به. كُتب هذا اللحن خصيصًا لهذه الأغنية على يد السير جورج جوب إيلفي في 1868 وأُعطي اسم Diademata. في اليونانية، تعني كلمة diademata «تجريدًا، تاجًا ملكيًا»—اسمٌ ملائمٌ لهذا اللحن الحماسي. يوافق عالم تاريخ الترانيم جي. ر. واتسون على هذا حين يلاحظ: «Diademata تهيئ إطارًا عظيمًا للنص، شبيهاً بالمسيرة ومبهجًا دون أن يصبح ميكانيكيًا أو صاخبًا.»

لعلّ جماعتنا تواصل ممارستها للترنيم الجماعي من كلّ القلب، رافعةً أصواتنا في التسبيح للرب في جمع القدّيسين! تاجّوه، ربّنا يسوع المسيح، بتيجانٍ كثيرة، لأنه مستحق!

The people we commonly refer to as the Russian Mennonites came into being as a group in a way quite similar to that of us with an Anabaptist heritage. We sprang from the same areas of Europe, from much of the same teachings of early Anabaptism, and have both experienced many of the same temptations and pitfalls, though at different times and locations.

This article will not focus on the beginnings of the Russian Mennonites apart from a brief overview. The group first entered Russia upon the urgings of the Viceroy Potemkin, who came into authority over the area now known as Ukraine after its annexation by Russia in 1783. The area had been under his partial administration since 1774, and he was eager to populate the land with foreign settlers. The residents of New Russia, as it was then called, were mostly nomads and Cossacks, a seminomadic group present in the steppes of Russia. The Mennonites in Danzig, Poland, were first approached with the offer of land, which would have appealed to them because they were routinely denied land ownership as a semi-persecuted people at that time. This offer came in August of 1786, and two brothers from the Danzig church were sent to survey the land and make arrangements for possible immigration.

The first immigration of 462 families began in 1788, and the “Old Colony” was established at Chortitza. They were afforded freedom of religion, exemption from military service, and the right to maintain their own schools and governances.

The Mennonites thrived in their new homeland. Although the first years were hard, partially due to the fact that mostly poorer families and those not in church leadership chose to resettle in Russia, the group soon began to transform the barren plains and steppes into rich agricultural communities. As the churches grew, so did their prosperity.

This period of relative peace lasted for over a century, until the late 1800s, when the Russian government, dissatisfied with the number of foreign settlements inside its borders, began applying pressure to many of the groups it had invited to settle its land some 100 years before. The Mennonites were not the only ones targeted, as many groups from various nations had established themselves in Russia. Steps taken against the Mennonites included pressure to participate in the armed forces as well as pressure to drop the German language that the communities had been using in favor of the Russian language. As these pressures increased, some Mennonites chose to flee the country in the 1870s. The majority, however, by now quite wealthy and affluent in comparison to their Russian peasant neighbors, chose to stay and weather the storm.

Unbeknownst to them, a full-scale revolution that would reshape Russia as a country was just around the corner. In 1917, the Bolsheviks came to power through the October Revolution, an event where the reigning tsar, or emperor, was deposed and exiled, and a new government was set up. A civil war broke out, and much of the fighting raged over the lands occupied by the Mennonites. Here, it is necessary to insert a brief history of the ideology of this new government.

The October Revolution and its subsequent change in government were fueled by a class war. As opposed to Nazi Germany, where a person could be arrested and killed for their race, in Russia, a person could and would be arrested for their class, for example, property ownership was seen as a crime against the people, and so the wealthier class of Russian peasants and farmers, those who most often owned property and employed the lower class of peasants, became an instant target a revolution that claimed to want to distribute all property and resources evenly amongst its citizenry.

By this time, the strong agricultural society of the Mennonites had transformed Ukraine into a breadbasket, its vast fields sown with wheat developed specifically by the Mennonites: Turkey Red Wheat. This hardy crop had made the Mennonite church quite wealthy, and their colonies had grown and flourished into villages of comfort and, at times, extravagance. This must have been a two-fold insult to the still impoverished peasants of Russia. Not only was there a large group of people in their midst that taught, spoke, and did their dealings in a language not of the Motherland, but these people also were wealthy beyond most peasants’ dreams.

It is, therefore, no surprise that when the kulaks, the wealthy class of peasants, came under persecution from the new government, the Mennonites were seen as the enemy of the people. As the civil war raged over Mennonite lands, villages were burnt and decimated, people executed or driven off, and livestock and grain plundered. Eventually, this period of fighting did come to an end, but for those few who survived the destruction, there was no reprieve to be found.

With the label of kulak and being generally defenseless, the Mennonites faced intense persecution. Religious services were rarely allowed, and the agricultural communities that had fed Russia and many others besides were collectivized and put under government control. Many of their churches ceased to exist entirely, although those in the east tended to last longer than the western villages.

Imagine then, to a people accustomed for generations to the favor and benevolence of material possessions and success, that all things material are stripped away. In a historical eye blink, the wealthy become the poor, and the favored become the hated. Even with a strong Christian faith, such a turn of events would shock and confuse.

But further tests were yet ahead for those who endured the first 25 years of the Soviet persecution. With the memory of their easy lives still fresh, the dawn of World War II brought a unique and enticing opportunity: the rise of a government that promoted the well-being of the German race, that valued those groups that could turn an empty prairie into a sprawling farm, that was vehemently anti-Communist- to this beleaguered group of believers, this must have seemed to be a God sent miracle to deliver them from their burdensome exile.

And so, they embraced the invading Germans. We readers, who are blessed with the ability to see the end result of these people’s decisions, can certainly make a good guess at what the end result was of wholesale support for the Nazis, but we must remember the scenarios that these Mennonites found themselves in...it was not one that would have been easy to decipher and decide upon if it were to be judged by man’s knowledge.

And so it was that the descendants of those helpless believers who gave their bodies at the stake and sword aligned themselves with a worldly kingdom that promised to protect and provide for them. In exchange for an eternal heritage, they chose to hope that the might of the German army would win back their earthly heritage and riches, and it was in this might that they trusted, forming bands of men who fought alongside the Germans against their old neighbors.

History did not deviate from its course, and the German army was eventually beaten back to its own borders and then further, and yet further into German lands. Before this retreating army ran those that had looked to it for their deliverance.

The atrocities of the Soviet government against its citizens are well documented in various works, most famously in the Gulag Archipelago, a book written by a Russian officer who was accused of treason. That author, Aleksandr Solzhenitsyn, painted a terrible picture of the treatment and exile of those who had opposed the USSR. Amongst the imprisoned or executed millions described in his tomes, there lie the remnants of a people who began as we did, experienced the smile of prosperity as we do, and then, treasuring that prosperity, lost it in calamitous fashion. We would do well to consider the paths we choose, as the wise king of the Scriptures instructs us, lest we, too, fall in the pursuit of prosperity. “Ponder the path of thy feet, and let all thy ways be established” (Proverbs 4:26).

De mensen die we gewoonlijk de Russische doopsgezinden noemen, zijn als groep ontstaan op een manier die behoorlijk vergelijkbaar is met die van ons met een anabaptistische erfenis. We kwamen voort uit dezelfde delen van Europa, uit veel van dezelfde leerstellingen van het vroege anabaptisme, en hebben allebei veel van dezelfde verzoekingen en valkuilen ervaren, al op andere tijden en plaatsen.

Dit artikel zal zich niet op de begindagen van de Russische doopsgezinden richten, behalve een korte overzichtsschets. De groep kwam voor het eerst Rusland binnen op aandringen van de viceroy Potemkin, die na de annexatie van het gebied dat nu Oekraïne heet in 1783 gezag over dat gebied kreeg. Het gebied viel sinds 1774 gedeeltelijk onder zijn bestuur, en hij was erop gebrand het land met buitenlandse kolonisten te bevolken. De bewoners van Nieuw-Rusland, zoals het toen genoemd werd, bestonden grotendeels uit nomaden en Kozakken, een seminomadische groep die in de steppen van Rusland aanwezig was. De doopsgezinden in Danzig, Polen, werden als eerste benaderd met het aanbod van land, wat aantrekkelijk voor hen zou zijn geweest omdat hen als een halfvervolgd volk in die tijd routinematig het eigendom van land werd ontzegd. Dit aanbod kwam in augustus 1786, en twee broeders van de Danzigse gemeente werden gestuurd om het land te inspecteren en regelingen te treffen voor mogelijke immigratie.

De eerste immigratie van 462 gezinnen begon in 1788, en de “Old Colony” werd gesticht bij Chortitza. Hun werd godsdienstvrijheid, vrijstelling van militaire dienst en het recht om hun eigen scholen en besturen te behouden toegekend.

De doopsgezinden gedijden in hun nieuwe vaderland. Hoewel de eerste jaren zwaar waren, deels doordat vooral armere gezinnen en degenen die niet in het kerkelijk bestuur zaten ervoor kozen zich in Rusland te vestigen, begon de groep spoedig de barre vlakten en steppen te transformeren tot rijke landbouwgemeenschappen. Naarmate de gemeenten groeiden, nam ook hun welvaart toe.

Deze periode van relatieve vrede duurde meer dan een eeuw, totdat in de late jaren 1800 de Russische regering, ontevreden over het aantal buitenlandse nederzettingen binnen haar grenzen, druk begon uit te oefenen op veel van de groepen die zij ongeveer 100 jaar eerder had uitgenodigd zich te vestigen. De doopsgezinden waren niet de enigen die het doelwit waren, want veel groepen uit verschillende landen hadden zich in Rusland gevestigd. Maatregelen tegen de doopsgezinden omvatten druk om deel te nemen aan de krijgsmacht en druk om de Duitse taal die de gemeenschappen gebruikten op te geven ten gunste van de Russische taal. Naarmate deze druk toenam, kozen sommige doopsgezinden ervoor het land te ontvluchten in de jaren 1870. De meerderheid echter, inmiddels tamelijk welvarend en vermogend vergeleken met hun Russische pachters, koos ervoor te blijven en de storm uit te zitten.

Onbekend aan hen stond een volledige revolutie die Rusland als land zou hervormen voor de deur. In 1917 kwamen de bolsjewieken via de Oktoberrevolutie aan de macht, een gebeurtenis waarbij de heersende tsaar, of keizer, werd afgezet en verbannen, en een nieuwe regering werd ingesteld. Een burgeroorlog brak uit, en veel van de gevechten woedden over de landen die door de doopsgezinden werden bewoond. Hier is het noodzakelijk een korte geschiedenis in te voegen van de ideologie van deze nieuwe regering.

De Oktoberrevolutie en de daaropvolgende machtswisseling werden gevoed door klassenstrijd. In tegenstelling tot nazi-Duitsland, waar iemand gearresteerd en gedood kon worden om zijn ras, kon en zou men in Rusland worden gearresteerd om zijn klasse; eigendom werd bijvoorbeeld gezien als een misdaad tegen het volk, en zo werden de rijkere klasse van Russische pachters en boeren, degenen die vaak eigendom bezaten en de lagere klasse pachters in dienst hadden, een onmiddellijk doelwit van een revolutie die beweerde alle eigendom en middelen gelijkmatig onder de burgers te willen verdelen.

Ondertussen had de sterke agrarische samenleving van de doopsgezinden Oekraïne veranderd in een graanschuur, met uitgestrekte velden ingezaaid met speciaal door de doopsgezinden ontwikkelde tarwe: Turkey Red Wheat. Deze sterke gewassoort had de doopsgezinde kerk behoorlijk rijk gemaakt, en hun kolonies waren uitgegroeid en welvarend geworden tot dorpen van comfort en soms weelde. Dit moet een dubbele belediging zijn geweest voor de nog steeds verarmde pachters van Rusland. Niet alleen was er een grote groep mensen onder hen die in een taal leefde, sprak en handelde die niet van het moederland was, maar deze mensen waren ook rijker dan de meeste pachters zich konden voorstellen.

Het is dan ook geen verrassing dat wanneer de kulakken, de rijke klasse van pachters, onder vervolging van de nieuwe regering kwamen te staan, de doopsgezinden als de vijand van het volk werden gezien. Terwijl de burgeroorlog over doopsgezinde landen woedde, werden dorpen in brand gestoken en verwoest, mensen geëxecuteerd of verdreven, en vee en graan geplunderd. Uiteindelijk kwam deze periode van gevechten tot een einde, maar voor de weinigen die de verwoesting overleefden, was er geen verlichting te vinden.

Met het etiket kulak en over het algemeen weerloos, werden de doopsgezinden intens vervolgd. Godsdienstoefeningen werden zelden toegestaan, en de landbouwgemeenschappen die Rusland en vele anderen hadden gevoed, werden gecollectiviseerd en onder regeringstoezicht geplaatst. Vele van hun kerken hielden geheel op te bestaan, hoewel die in het oosten de neiging hadden langer te blijven bestaan dan de westelijke dorpen.

Stel u dan voor, voor een volk dat generaties lang gewend was aan de gunst en weldadigheid van materiële bezittingen en succes, dat alle materiële zaken worden weggenomen. In een historische oogwenk worden de rijken arm en de bevoorrechten gehaten. Zelfs met een sterk christelijk geloof zou zo’n ommekeer schokkend en verwarrend zijn.

Maar verdere beproevingen stonden nog voor degenen die de eerste 25 jaar van de Sovjetvervolging doorstonden. Met de herinnering aan hun gemakkelijke levens nog vers, bracht de aanvang van de Tweede Wereldoorlog een unieke en verleidelijke kans: de opkomst van een regering die het welzijn van het Duitse ras promootte, die die groepen waardeerde die een lege prairie in een uitgestrekte boerderij konden veranderen, die fel anti-communistisch was — voor deze geplaagde groep gelovigen moet dit als een door God gezonden wonder zijn verschenen om hen te verlossen van hun zware ballingschap.

En zo omarmden ze de binnenvallende Duitsers. Wij lezers, die de afloop van de beslissingen van deze mensen kunnen overzien, kunnen zeker een goede gok doen naar het uiteindelijke resultaat van het massale steunbetuigen aan de nazi’s, maar we moeten ons de scenario’s herinneren waarin deze doopsgezinden zich bevonden... het was niet iets dat gemakkelijk te doorzien en te beoordelen zou zijn op grond van menselijk inzicht.

En zo sloten de nakomelingen van die weerloze gelovigen die hun lichamen aan het vuur en zwaard hadden prijsgegeven zich aan bij een werelds koninkrijk dat beloofde hen te beschermen en te voorzien. In ruil voor een eeuwig erfdeel kozen zij te hopen dat de macht van het Duitse leger hun aardse erfgoed en rijkdommen zou terugwinnen, en op die macht vertrouwden zij, en vormden groepen mannen die samen met de Duitsers tegen hun oude buren vochten.

De geschiedenis week niet af van haar loop, en het Duitse leger werd uiteindelijk teruggedrongen tot zijn eigen grenzen en daarna verder, en nog verder, het land van de Duitsers binnen. Voor dit terugtrekkende leger vluchtten degenen die in het hunnen voor hun bevrijding hadden gekeken.

De wreedheden van de Sovjetregering tegen haar burgers zijn goed gedocumenteerd in verschillende werken, het bekendst misschien in De Goelagarchipel, een boek geschreven door een Russische officier die van verraad werd beschuldigd. Die auteur, Aleksandr Solzhenitsyn, schetste een afschuwelijk beeld van de behandeling en uitzetting van degenen die zich tegen de USSR verzetten. Te midden van de miljoenen gevangenen of geëxecuteerden die in zijn geschriften beschreven worden, liggen de resten van een volk dat begon zoals wij deden, dat de glimlach van welvaart ervoer zoals wij, en dat toen, die welvaart koesterend, die op rampzalige wijze verloor. We doen er goed aan de paden die we kiezen te overwegen, zoals de wijze koning der Schriften ons opdraagt, opdat ook wij niet in de jacht naar welvaart vallen. “Overweeg het pad van uw voeten, en laat al uw wegen wel behouwd zijn” (Spreuken 4:26).

“O the depth of the riches both of the wisdom and knowledge of God! how unsearchable are His judgments, and his ways past finding out! For who hath known the mind of the Lord? Or who hath been his counsellor? Or who hath first given to him, and it shall be recompensed unto him again? For of Him, and through Him, and to him, are all things: to whom be glory for ever. Amen” (Rom. 11:33–36).

What an exuberant and expressive exclamation written by Apostle Paul! As we look at a new hymn and hymn writer again, let’s keep our minds alert and hearts open to see the hand of God at work.

Matthew Bridges was born at Malden, Essex, in England, on July 14, 1800. He began to publish verses in 1825 and continued until he had published two small volumes of hymns—Hymns of the Heart (1848) and The Passion of Jesus (1852). From here, I will continue with the story by giving a brief history of the church life of our hymnodist.

The hymn writer we are studying in this article was a part of the Anglican Church of England. Around the middle of the 19th century, he became dissatisfied with the church group he was with and found himself following the leading of John Henry Newman in what was called the Oxford Movement. According to hymnologist Albert Bailey, this movement centered on, “Claiming for their Anglican Church lineal descent from the original Apostolic Church.” In pursuit of this, the organization’s followers studied the ancient history of the church, its doctrine, and especially its liturgy. In doing so, they discovered a wealth of Greek and Latin hymnody from the earliest centuries of the Christian church.

As sadly, we find many factions in the Christian church today, so also was the scope of things going on in the mid–1800s. The Oxford Movement seemed in some ways to be a competition between the old and the new way of doing things. In the case of the figure in our story today, it seems he saw a more stable path forward in keeping the old traditions of the mother church, yet he also seemed to have a real, living faith in our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ. Now, I want to interject here that I trust his decision was made in all good conscience toward God, even though we look on today from an Anabaptist viewpoint and question his reasons for doing so.

We will continue with our story here. Matthew Bridges converted to Roman Catholicism and, wanting to share in the rich hymnic tradition of the Protestant Church, began writing original hymns. Mr. Bridges’ hymns are marked by spirituality and genuine power. One of his hymns we love and enjoy is “Rise, Glorious Conqueror.” Undoubtedly, his greatest hymn is “Crown Him with Many Crowns.” It first appeared in his book The Passion of Jesus, and was originally given the title “The Song of the Seraphs.”

There is an interesting background connected to this hymn, including how there came to be 12 verses. Understandably, only a portion of those verses are being sung today. The selection of verses depends on the hymnal.

Matthew Bridges originally penned the song in 1851. He wrote six stanzas, all based upon Rev. 19:12: “ ... and on His head were many crowns.” The edition by Bridges continued until the 1870s when a devout Anglican clergyman named Godfrey Thring came along. Godfrey was concerned that this popular hymn allowed catholic theology to be sung by protestant congregations. His concerns centered perhaps on Bridges’ original second verse, where he referenced the Blessed Virgin Mary. In light of this, Thring wrote six new stanzas and published it in his Hymns and Sacred Lyrics in 1874.

The 12 stanzas have been mixed and matched down through the years. Interestingly, of the six verses most commonly appearing in hymnals today, three were written by Bridges and three by Thring. The hymn, as published in the Hymns of the Church songbook, completely omits original verse 2 and uses verses 1, 3, 4, part of 5, and part of 6 out of Bridges’ original six verses. The stanzas we sing in that book are highlighted in the selection of verses below. Also included as well are the six couplets by Thring.

Crown Him with Many Crowns

—Bridges

Crown Him with many crowns, the Lamb upon His throne;
Hark! how the heavenly anthems drowns all music but its own;
Awake, my soul, and sing of Him who died for thee,
And hail Him as thy matchless King through all eternity.

Crown Him the Virgin’s Son! The God Incarnate born—
Whose arm those crimson trophies won which now His brow adorn!
Fruit of the mystic Rose as of that Rose the Stem:
The Root, whence mercy ever flows—the Babe of Bethlehem!

Crown Him the Lord of peace! Whose power a scepter sways,
From pole to pole, that wars may cease, absorbed in prayer and praise:
His reign shall know no end, and round His pierced feet
Fair flowers of paradise extend their fragrance ever sweet.

Crown Him the Lord of love! Behold His hands and side—
Rich wounds, yet visible above, in beauty glorified:
No angel in the sky can fully bear that sight,
But downward bends his burning eye at mysteries so bright!

Crown Him the Lord of years! The Potentate of time—
Creator of the rolling spheres, ineffably sublime!
Glassed in a sea of light, where everlasting waves
Reflect His throne—the Infinite! Who lives—and loves—and saves.

Crown Him the Lord of heaven! One with the Father known,
And the blest Spirit, through Him given from yonder triune throne!
All hail! Redeemer—Hail! For Thou hast died for me;
Thy praise shall never, never fail throughout eternity!

Crown Him with Many Crowns

—Thring

Crown Him with crowns of gold, all nations great and small,
Crown Him, ye martyred saints of old, the Lamb once slain for all;
The Lamb once slain for them who bring their praises now,
As jewels for the diadem that girds His sacred brow.

Crown Him the Son of God before the worlds began,
And ye, who tread where He hath trod, crown Him the Son of man;
Who every grief hath known that wrings the human breast,
And takes and bears them for His own, that all in Him may rest.

Crown Him the Lord of light, Who o’er a darkened world
In robes of glory infinite His fiery flag unfurled.
And bore it raised on high, in heaven—in earth—beneath,
To all the sign of victory o’er Satan, sin, and death.

Crown Him the Lord of life Who triumphed o’er the grave,
And rose victorious in the strife for those He came to save;
His glories now we sing Who died, and rose on high.
Who died, eternal life to bring and lives that death may die.

Crown Him of lords the Lord, Who over all doth reign
Who once on earth, the incarnate Word, for ransomed sinners slain,
Now lives in realms of light, where saints with angels sing
Their songs before Him day and night, their God, Redeemer, King.

Crown Him the Lord of heaven, enthroned in worlds above;
Crown Him the King, to whom is given the wondrous name of Love,
Crown Him with many crowns, as thrones before Him fall.
Crown Him, ye kings, with many crowns, for He is King of all.

Matthew Bridges lived his latter years in the province of Quebec, Canada, then returned to England before his passing from earth on October 6, 1894, at the ripe old age of 94. Although we don’t find many details about his life, he has left one of the greatest hymns in our hands today.

A great part of this song’s enduring quality is the tune it is paired with. This refrain was written especially for this song by Sir George Job Elvey in 1868 and was given the name of Diademata. In Greek, the word diademata means “a royal crown”—a fitting name for this stirring melody. Hymnology scholar J. R. Watson agrees with this when he observes, “Diademata makes a magnificent setting for the text, march-like and joyful without ever becoming mechanical or strident.”

May our congregations continue our practice of corporate, whole-hearted singing, lifting our voices in praise to the Lord in the assembly of the saints! Crown Him, our Lord Jesus Christ, with many crowns, for he is worthy!

«O dybden av rikdommen både i Guds visdom og kunnskap! Hvor uforsonlige er hans dommer, og hans veier uutforskelige! For hvem har kjent Herrens sinn? Eller hvem har vært hans rådgiver? Eller hvem har først gitt ham, og det skal bli gjengjeldt ham igjen? For av ham, og gjennom ham, og til ham er alle ting: ham være ære i evighet. Amen» (Rom. 11:33–36).

For et utsynsrikt og uttrykksfullt utrop skrevet av apostelen Paulus! Når vi igjen ser på en ny salme og en salmedikter, la oss holde våre sinn våkne og våre hjerter åpne for å se Guds hånd i arbeid.

Matthew Bridges ble født i Malden, Essex, i England, den 14. juli 1800. Han begynte å publisere vers i 1825 og fortsatte til han hadde utgitt to små bind med salmer—Hymns of the Heart (1848) og The Passion of Jesus (1852). Herfra vil jeg fortsette historien ved å gi en kort oversikt over salmedikterens kirkelige liv.

Salmedikteren vi studerer i denne artikkelen var en del av den anglikanske kirken i England. Omkring midten av 1800-tallet ble han misfornøyd med kirkesamfunnet han tilhørte og fulgte ledelsen til John Henry Newman i det som ble kalt Oxfordbevegelsen. Ifølge hymnologen Albert Bailey sentrerte denne bevegelsen seg om «å gjøre krav på at deres anglikanske kirke hadde direkte avstamning fra den opprinnelige apostoliske kirke.» I jakten på dette studerte bevegelsens tilhengere kirkens eldste historie, dens lære, og spesielt dens liturgi. I prosessen oppdaget de et rike av gresk og latinsk salmeskatt fra de tidligste århundrene av den kristne kirke.

Like trist som det er at vi finner mange bruddstykker i den kristne kirke i dag, var også omfanget av ting som skjedde midt på 1800-tallet. Oxfordbevegelsen synes på noen måter å ha vært en konkurranse mellom den gamle og den nye måten å gjøre ting på. I tilfellet med skikkelsen i vår historie i dag, ser det ut til at han så en mer stabil vei fremover i å bevare mor kirkens gamle tradisjoner, samtidig som han også synes å ha hatt en ekte, levende tro på vår Herre og Frelser Jesus Kristus. Jeg vil her innskyte at jeg stoler på at hans beslutning ble tatt i god samvittighet overfor Gud, selv om vi i dag fra et anabaptistisk synspunkt stiller spørsmål ved hans grunner for å gjøre det.

Vi går videre med historien her. Matthew Bridges konverterte til den romersk-katolske kirke og, ønskende å ta del i den rike hymntradisjonen fra den protestantiske kirke, begynte å skrive originale salmer. Mr. Bridges’ salmer kjennetegnes av åndelighet og ekte kraft. En av hans salmer vi elsker og nyter er «Rise, Glorious Conqueror.» Utvilsomt er hans største salme «Crown Him with Many Crowns.» Den dukket først opp i hans bok The Passion of Jesus, og ble opprinnelig gitt tittelen «The Song of the Seraphs.»

Det er en interessant bakgrunn knyttet til denne salmen, inkludert hvordan den kom til å få 12 vers. Forståelig nok blir bare en del av disse versene sunget i dag. Utvalget av vers avhenger av salmeboken.

Matthew Bridges skrev opprinnelig sangen i 1851. Han skrev seks strofer, alle basert på Åp. 19:12: «... og på hans hode var mange kroner.» Bridges’ utgave fortsatte til 1870-årene da en from anglikansk prest ved navn Godfrey Thring dukket opp. Godfrey var bekymret for at denne populære salmen tillot katolsk teologi å bli sunget av protestantiske menigheter. Hans bekymringer dreide seg trolig om Bridges’ opprinnelige andre vers, hvor han refererte til den salige jomfru Maria. I lys av dette skrev Thring seks nye strofer og publiserte dem i sin Hymns and Sacred Lyrics i 1874.

De 12 strofene har blitt blandet og matchet gjennom årene. Interessant nok av de seks versene som oftest forekommer i dagens salmebøker, var tre skrevet av Bridges og tre av Thring. Salmen, som publisert i sangboken Hymns of the Church, utelater fullstendig opprinnelig vers 2 og bruker vers 1, 3, 4, del av 5 og del av 6 fra Bridges’ opprinnelige seks vers. Strofer vi synger i den boken er markert i utvalget av vers nedenfor. Også inkludert er de seks parstrofene av Thring.

Crown Him with Many Crowns

—Bridges

Kron ham med mange kroner, Lammet på hans trone;
Hør! hvordan de himmelske anthemer drukner all musikk uten sin egen;
Våkn opp, min sjel, og syng om Ham som døde for deg,
Og hils Ham som din uovertrufne Konge gjennom all evighet.

Kron Ham, Marias Sønn! Gud inkarnert født—
Hvis arm vant de purpurrøde trofeene som nå pryder hans panne!
Frukt av den mystiske Rose liksom av den Roses Stamme:
Røtten, hvorfra miskunn alltid flyter—Bethlehems Barn!

Kron Ham, fredens Herre! Hvis makt svinger et septer,
Fra pol til pol, så kriger må ta slutt, oppslukt i bønn og pris:
Hans regjering skal kjenne ingen ende, og rundt hans gjennomborende føtter
Utstrekker paradisets skjønne blomster sin duft evig søt.

Kron Ham, kjærlighetens Herre! Se hans hender og side—
Rike sår, likevel synlige over, i skjønnhet forherliget:
Ingen engel på himmelen kan fullt bære det syn,
Men bøyer sitt brennende øye ned ved mysterier så klare!

Kron Ham, årens Herre! Tidens Mægtige—
Skaperen av de rullende sfærer, uutsigelig sublimer!
Innkapslet i et hav av lys, hvor evige bølger
Reflekterer hans trone—den Uendelige! Som lever—og elsker—og frelser.

Kron Ham, himmelens Herre! Én med Faderen kjent,
Og den salige Ånd, gjennom Ham gitt fra den treenige trone der borte!
All helsning! Frelser—Hils! For Du har dødd for meg;
Din pris skal aldri, aldri svikte gjennom evigheten!

Crown Him with Many Crowns

—Thring

Kron Ham med gullkroner, alle nasjoner store og små,
Krone Ham, dere martyriske helgener fra gammel tid, Lammet en gang slaktet for alle;
Lammet som en gang ble slaktet for dem som nå bringer sine lovsanger,
Som juveler for diademet som omgir hans hellige panne.

Kron Ham, Guds Sønn, før verdener begynte,
Og dere som trår hvor Han har trampet, krone Ham Menneskesønnen;
Han som har kjent enhver sorg som vrir menneskehjertet,
Og tar dem og bærer dem som sine egne, for at alle i Ham må finne hvile.

Kron Ham, lysets Herre, Som over en tilslørt verden
I herlighetens uendelige kapper rullet sitt brennende banner ut.
Og bar det hevet høyt, i himmel—på jord—under,
Til alle som tegn på seier over Satan, synd og død.

Kron Ham, livets Herre, Som triumferte over graven,
Og stod seirende opp i striden for dem Han kom for å frelse;
Hans herligheter synger vi nå Som døde, og stod opp på høydet.
Som døde for å bringe evig liv og lever for at døden må dø.

Kron Ham herrenes Herre, Som over alle rår
Som en gang på jorden, det inkarnate Ord, for løsepengede syndere ble drept,
Nå lever i lysets riker, hvor hellige sammen med engler synger
Deres sanger for Ham dag og natt, deres Gud, Frelser, Konge.

Kron Ham, himmelens Herre, innsatt i verdener ovenfor;
Kron Ham Kongen, som har fått det underfulle navn Kjærlighet,
Kron Ham med mange kroner, så troner faller foran Ham.
Kron Ham, dere konger, med mange kroner, for Han er alles Konge.

Matthew Bridges tilbrakte sine siste år i provinsen Quebec, Canada, og vendte så tilbake til England før han forlot denne verden den 6. oktober 1894, i en høy alder av 94 år. Selv om vi ikke finner mange detaljer om hans liv, har han etterlatt oss en av de største salmene vi har i dag.

En stor del av denne sangens varige kvalitet ligger i melodien den er satt til. Denne refrengen ble skrevet spesielt for denne sangen av Sir George Job Elvey i 1868 og fikk navnet Diademata. På gresk betyr ordet diademata «en kongelig krone»—et passende navn for denne gripende melodien. Hymnologisk forsker J. R. Watson er enig i dette når han observerer, «Diademata gir en storslått ramme til teksten, marsjaktig og glad uten noensinne å bli mekanisk eller skarp.»

Må våre menigheter fortsette vår praksis med fellessang, helhjertet, løftende våre stemmer i lovsang til Herren i de helliges forsamling! Kron Ham, vår Herre Jesus Kristus, med mange kroner, for han er verdig!

Kilder: A Treasury of Hymn Stories, hymnary.org, umc-discipleship.org, FBC

What do we think about when we think of the term ‘church’? We live in a day when there are many and varied churches. If one church doesn’t suit you, there are others to choose from. While some churches encourage their people to live for God and others instead of themselves, other churches promote a gospel that says lots of money and a better life now are the results of following Christ. However, there are still churches that try to follow what the Bible says—Sola scriptura (scripture alone). Traditionally, the conservative Anabaptist churches in America have tried to function in this manner. But is that changing?

We live in a day when lines are being crossed, blurred, and confused. People aren’t sure what is true and what is not. Today, men and women around the world are looking for answers and solutions, but where should they look?

I was talking with a young man who testified of being converted at a young age. He attended church faithfully and was considered quite gifted. But there was a problem—he had a sin that he still could not control. As he wrestled with God and pled for victory, he began to hear a recurring message from other professing Christians, “No one is perfect!” “We all have issues.” “Everyone has sinned!” Finally, this young man accepted his sin as normal. He justified it because it seemed that everyone was saying they had sin also, that they were not living in complete victory. It led this young man to a place of complete ruin.

Are we preaching and accepting a defeated Gospel—a gospel that doesn’t offer complete forgiveness and complete victory? Many youth of today are confused. Many people in today’s world don’t understand. Anyone can go to church and try to be a better person. But what about the all-powerful, life-changing gospel of Jesus Christ?

The apostle Paul says that Jesus is coming back for “. . .a glorious church, not having spot, or wrinkle, or any such thing; but that it should be holy and without blemish” (Eph. 5:27). And Jesus Himself said “. . .That thou art Peter, and upon this rock I will build my church; and the gates of hell shall not prevail against it” (Matt. 16:18).

Before I was converted, I was certainly a slave to sin, but I wanted victory. I was addicted to drugs and alcohol, but I didn’t like it. I wanted to be free. I went to counseling and rehab facilities all over America, but it didn’t work. I had no power. I could quit for a few days or even weeks, then anger and depression would set in, and I would return to the substances. One day, I came face to face with the Creator. The hand of the almighty God got ahold of me and opened my eyes. I repented of my sins and was given a clean slate and a clean heart. I never went back. Drugs, alcohol, and two packs of cigarettes a day were finished—forever.

I could hardly believe what God was doing. The power of God was real. I could not overcome it by myself, as none of us can, but God has promised us freedom from bondage and a new life of victorious living if we submit our lives to him. This ability to overcome the power of sin and then walk in victory is what the world is looking for. Do we believe that God can free us not only from substance abuse but also from anger, selfishness, bitterness, greed, and pride? God’s Word says “If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins, and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness” (1 John 1:9). No one is interested in a defeated Gospel, no one except those who are living in defeat because they have chosen the things of this world over God and His Word.

Are we willing to testify of the power of the resurrection? We need to proclaim a gospel that completely saves people from the bondage of sin—forever. We must be bold and confident in our faith so we can lead people to the Master.

I was witnessing to a man when he said in a rather loud voice, “God is not real!” My six-year-old son’s mouth fell open, and he gasped, “Daddy, he just told a lie!”

My son doesn’t need to be convinced that God is real; he believes it with all his heart. The world out there does need to be convinced. They need to see something that science cannot explain. They need to see something that defies all odds.

That something is a heart that has been truly changed. The fighter now loves his enemies. The person with an anger problem now loves others unconditionally. Broken families are healed. Wretched sinners are forgiven and living a transformed life. Hope, peace, love, and power are freely given to men and women who seemingly have no hope. “The blind receive their sight, and the lame walk, the lepers are cleansed, and the deaf hear, the dead are raised up, and the poor have the gospel preached to them ” (Matt. 11:5).

Are you living your life so the world can see the work of God being practical, effective, and real every day? Here are a few things the Church needs in our day to once again draw in the lost.

A willingness to suffer

History would show that the church, all through the ages, has suffered for Christ. It was part of the cost of following Christ. The Bible says, “Yea, and all that will live godly in Christ Jesus shall suffer persecution” (2 Tim. 3:12). It was something that just happened.

Today, many people want the American dream. Folks live a good moral life, are good citizens, make a good living, and go to church on Sundays. But is that what we are called to? The gospel spread like wildfire when the church suffered persecution and did so willingly and joyfully. It was something the world had never seen—a faith that people showed by their life, and their death was something worth dying for. Let’s not be afraid to suffer for Christ today.

Denial of self

Then said Jesus unto his disciples, “If any man will come after me, let him deny himself, and take up his cross, and follow me” (Matt. 16:24).

Have you ever wondered why Jesus instructs us to deny ourselves? After all, He gave us desires and passions, so why must we deny them? I have heard people say that we need to align our will with God’s, but I do not find this in the Bible. Rather, we should simply deny our will and accept God’s will.

I remember the first day of boot camp when I joined the Marine Corps after graduating from high school. Close to one hundred young men were there. We all had our own desires and thoughts. We had our own identity. It was amazing to see all the diversity. It would have been a disaster if the United States of America had sent us off to battle that first day. So, they had a plan set in place to fix this problem. Over the next three months, they broke us. Physically and mentally, we learned how to deny ourselves and submit to our commanders and each other. The world is often amazed by the great discipline and unity for which the Marines are known.

When we become a part of the kingdom of God, we cannot be effective if we each do what we want. A body of believers can all have good intentions, but if any one person has not denied themselves, they will never be able to submit to the greater cause. There is a war raging, and we cannot fight it alone. We must deny ourselves, join forces with our brethren, and fight for victory in our homes, churches, and lives.

Submission

The Bible calls us to submit ourselves:

  • to God (Jas. 4:7).
  • [to those] that have the [spiritual] rule over you [us] (Heb. 13:17).
  • to every ordinance of man for the Lord’s sake (1 Pet. 2:13).
  • one to another in the fear of God (Eph. 5:21).

Once we deny ourselves, then and only then, can we submit to others. Many people today have great difficulty in submitting to their fellow man. Some feel they are free in Christ; therefore, they can do as they please. There is a reason why we are instructed to submit to others. It is easy for us to drift away from sound doctrine when we believe we can figure everything out on our own.

When we have truly denied ourselves, we find that it is rather easy, and even a great blessing, to submit to the brotherhood. In fact, it is true freedom. What you want doesn’t matter, and you begin to depend on your brothers and sisters. When getting our own way isn’t important to us, then when we don’t get our way, we are fine with it. As we lay down our lives for each other, we become a force that the world doesn’t understand. The world was drawn to the church for centuries, wanting what it had. But amazingly, today, it seems the church is being drawn to the world, wanting what it has.

There is power in submission. Hundreds of years ago, a man named Alexander the Great conquered almost all of the then-known world using military strength and cleverness mixed with diplomacy.

The story is told that Alexander and a small company of soldiers approached a strongly fortified, walled city. Standing outside the walls, Alexander raised his voice and demanded to see the king. When the king arrived, Alexander insisted that the king surrender the city and its inhabitants to Alexander and his little band of fighting men.

The king laughed, “Why should I surrender to you? You can’t do us any harm!” So, Alexander offered to give the king a demonstration. He ordered his men to line up single file and start marching. He marched them straight toward a sheer cliff.

The townspeople gathered on the wall and watched in shocked silence as, one by one, Alexander’s soldiers marched, without hesitation, right off the cliff to their deaths! After ten soldiers died, Alexander ordered the rest of the men to return to his side. The townspeople and the king immediately surrendered to Alexander the Great. They realized that if a few men were actually willing to commit suicide at the command of this dynamic leader, then nothing could stop his eventual victory.

Obedience

Submission and obedience go hand in hand. If we are willing to submit to something or someone, we will want to obey it. It becomes very important to submit to those who are over us, especially the almighty God in Heaven. If we struggle to submit, we will usually struggle with obedience. God forbid if we begin to believe that we are better off doing things alone without our brothers.

Love

“By this shall all men know that ye are my disciples, if ye have love one to another” (John 13:35).

People wave to each other at an intersection, or they will open the door for an elderly person. People are generally loving people until something doesn’t go their way. Then they can become very difficult. Is that the way the church today is showing its love to the world? As long as everything is going smoothly, and no one steps on our toes, we all get along and we love each other. Then as soon as there is something worth fighting over, we put the “boxing gloves” on. Doesn’t the Bible say that “charity (love) beareth all things, believeth all things, hopeth all things, endureth all things” (1 Cor. 13:7)? True love is revealed when we face adversity or when a brother does something to offend us. That is the love that will show the world we are disciples of Jesus.

Do we love our brother enough to help when he is in need? Maybe he is unknowingly straying away from God in a certain area. How much do we love him? Some people think that love is only talking about positive things with each other, but if we truly love our brother, we will go to him in love and speak honestly with him. Then if we are practicing a lifestyle of denying ourselves and submitting to the brethren, it should go well. God forbid if we get angry with a brother who comes to us to show us our error.

When we have chosen to suffer with the people of God and have denied ourselves, then we appreciate when a brother or sister speaks into our lives. We will not allow ourselves to become offended.

Suffering for and with each other, plus denying ourselves for each other, often forms a solid love for one another. This type of love is the kind that the world around us does not know but desires greatly. The world is getting more selfish and independent as the days pass. We can’t afford to miss our opportunities to show them the power of God with our love for one another.

Godly people throughout the ages have had their opportunity to serve the King and spread the message of the Kingdom of God, but they have moved on to eternity. Today it is our turn. The fields are white unto harvest. Let’s plug in and, with God’s help, preserve the glorious church of Jesus Christ for our children, the next generation.

当我们想到“教会”这个词时，会想到什么？我们生活在一个教会众多且各式各样的时代。如果某个教会不适合你，还有其他教会可供选择。有些教会鼓励他们的会众为神而活，而不是为自己；另一些教会却宣扬一种福音，称追随基督会带来大量金钱和更好的现世生活。然而，仍有教会试图遵循圣经所说——唯独经上（Sola scriptura）。从传统上看，美国保守的再洗礼派（Anabaptist）教会一直努力以这种方式运作。但这种状况是否在改变？

我们生活在一个界线被跨越、模糊和混淆的时代。人们不确定什么是真，什么是假。如今，世界各地的男女都在寻找答案和解决之道，但他们应当到哪里去寻找？

我曾与一位年轻人交谈，他作证说年纪轻时就已归信。他忠心参加教会，被认为颇有恩赐。但有一个问题——他有一个仍无法控制的罪。当他与神争战并恳求得胜时，他开始从其他自称基督徒的人那里听到重复的信息，“没有人是完美的！”“我们都有问题。”“人人都有罪！”最终，这位年轻人接受了自己的罪是正常的。他辩解说似乎大家都在说他们也有罪，都没有活在完全的得胜之中。这使这位年轻人走向了彻底的毁灭。

我们是在宣讲并接受一个失败的福音吗——一个不提供完全赦免与完全得胜的福音？今天的许多青年感到困惑。如今世界上的许多人不明白。任何人都可以去教会并尽力做个更好的人。但耶稣基督那全能、能改变生命的福音怎么办？

使徒保罗说耶稣是为“……要用圣洁洁净的教会，毫无玷污、皱纹等类的病，乃要使她成为圣洁没有瑕疵”（弗5:27）。耶稣自己也说“……你是彼得，我要把我的教会建造在这磐石上，阴间的权柄不能胜过他”（太16:18）。

在我归信之前，我无疑是罪的奴仆，但我渴望得胜。我沉溺于毒品和酒精，但我不喜欢那样的生活。我想得自由。我去过美国各地的咨询和戒毒机构，但都没有用。我没有能力。我可以戒掉几天甚至几周，然后愤怒和沮丧就会来临，我又回到那些东西。一日，我直面造物主。全能神的手抓住我，打开了我的眼睛。我为我的罪悔改，得到了新的开始和洁净的心。我再也没有回头。毒品、酒精和每天两包香烟都结束了——永远结束。

我几乎不敢相信神所做的。神的能力是真实的。我自己无法战胜，就如我们没有一个人能凭自己做到，但神应许我们，只要我们将生命归服于他，就能从捆绑中得自由，过着得胜的新生活。这种战胜罪的能力并行在得胜中，就是世人所寻求的。你是否相信神不仅能救我们脱离药物滥用，也能救我们脱离愤怒、自私、苦毒、贪婪和骄傲？神的话说：“我们若认自己的罪，上帝是信实的，是公义的，要赦免我们的罪，洗净我们一切的不义”（约壹1:9）。除了那些选择今世的事物胜过神和他的话语而活在失败中的人外，没有人会对失败的福音感兴趣。

我们愿意为复活的大能作见证吗？我们需要宣扬一种完全拯救人、使人永远脱离罪捆绑的福音。我们必须在信心上大胆和自信，以便能把人引到救主面前。

我曾向一名男子传道，他却相当大声地说：“神不真实！”我六岁的儿子目瞪口呆，喘息着说：“爸爸，他刚才说了谎！”

我的儿子不需要被说服神是真实的；他全心相信。外面的世界确实需要被说服。他们需要看到科学无法解释的事。他们需要看到那种违背一切概率的事。

那就是一个真正改变了的心。曾经好斗的人现在爱他的仇敌。曾有愤怒问题的人现在无条件地爱人。破碎的家庭得着医治。可怜的罪人得赦免并活出改变后的生命。没有指望的人得着盼望、平安、爱与能力，“瞎子得看见，瘸子行走，长大麻风的得洁净，聋子听见，死人复活，穷人有福音传给他们”（太11:5）。

你是否如此生活，使世人能看见神的作为在日常中是切实、有效且真实的？以下是当代教会需要的一些事，使我们能再次吸引失丧的人。

愿意受苦

历史会表明，教会在历代为基督受苦。这是跟随基督的代价之一。圣经说：“凡立志在基督耶稣里敬虔度日的，也都要受逼迫”（提后3:12）。这是自然而然会发生的事。

今天，许多人渴望美国梦。人们过着良好的道德生活，是好公民，谋生有道，周日去教会。但那真的是我们的呼召吗？当教会甘心并喜乐地为主受逼迫时，福音像野火般传播开来。世人从未见过那样的情形——人们用生命来显明信心，他们的死是值得为之而死的事。今天我们不要害怕为基督受苦。

否认自己

于是耶稣对门徒说：“若有人要跟从我，就当舍己，背起他的十字架来跟从我”（太16:24）。

你是否曾想过为何耶稣要我们舍己？毕竟，他赐给我们欲望与热情，为什么我们必须舍弃它们？我听过有人说我们需要使我们的意志与神的意旨对齐，但我在圣经中并未发现这说法。相反，我们应当单纯舍弃我们的意志，接受神的旨意。

我记得高中毕业后参军、进入海军陆战队训练营的第一天。近百名青年在那里。我们各有欲望和想法，有各自的身份认同。看到这些多样性令人惊讶。如果美利坚合众国在第一天就把我们送去打仗，那将是一场灾难。因此，他们有一套计划来解决这个问题。在接下来的三个月里，他们把我们“摧毁”——身心上，我们学会了如何舍己并服从我们的指挥官与彼此。世人常为海军陆战队那极大的纪律性与团结所惊叹。

当我们成为神的国度的一部分时，如果各人都随自己的意思行事，我们就无法有效地作为见证。一个信徒群体都可能怀有良好意图，但如果任何一人未曾舍己，他永远无法服从更大的使命。有一场争战正在进行，我们无法单独作战。我们必须舍己，与弟兄姊妹联手，在我们的家庭、教会和生命中争取得胜。

顺服

圣经呼召我们去顺服：

  • 顺服神（雅各书4:7）。
  • 顺服那些在你们身上有属灵权柄的人（来13:17）。
  • 为主的缘故，顺服各人的制度（彼前2:13）。
  • 在敬畏神的心里彼此顺服（弗5:21）。

只有当我们舍己之后，我们才能顺服别人。如今许多人在顺服同胞方面有很大困难。有些人觉得他们在基督里得了自由，因此可以为所欲为。我们被命令顺服众人的其中有其理由。当我们认为可以独自搞定一切时，很容易偏离正统教义。

当我们真心舍己时，会发现顺服弟兄姊妹其实相当容易，甚至是极大的福分。事实上，那是真正的自由。你想要什么并不重要，你开始依靠你的弟兄姊妹。当获得个人私欲不再重要时，我们在不能如愿时也心安理得。当我们为彼此舍命时，我们就成为一个世人难以理解的力量。几个世纪以来，世人被教会所吸引，渴望拥有教会所具有的。但令人惊讶的是，今天似乎是教会被世界所吸引，渴望拥有世界所具有的。

顺服有能力。几百年前，有一位名叫亚历山大大帝的人，凭借军力与机智并结合外交，征服了当时几乎已知的全世界。

故事讲到亚历山大和一小队士兵来到一座设防严密的城邑外。他站在城墙外，高声命令人见国王。国王到来后，亚历山大坚持要求国王将城池及其居民交出给他和他那小股战士。

国王大笑道：“我为何要向你投降？你伤害不了我们！”于是，亚历山大提出给国王一个示范。他命令士兵排成单列行进。他就带着他们直向一个险峻的悬崖前进。

城里的人聚集在城墙上，震惊地看着亚历山大的士兵们一个接一个地毫不犹豫地走下悬崖，掉到深渊而死！在十名士兵死亡后，亚历山大命令其余的人退回到他身边。城里的人和国王立刻向亚历山大大帝投降。他们意识到，如果有些人真的愿意在这位有魄力的领袖命令下自杀，那么没有什么可以阻止他最终的胜利。

顺从

顺服与顺从密不可分。如果我们愿意顺服某人或某事，就会愿意顺从它。向在我们之上的人，尤其是天上的全能神，顺服就显得极其重要。如果我们连顺服都挣扎，我们通常也会在顺从上有困难。若我们开始相信离开弟兄独自行动更好，愿上帝禁止这种想法。

爱

“人若有彼此相爱的心，众人因此就认出你们是我的门徒了”（约13:35）。

人们在路口互相招手，或为年长者开门。人在一般情况下是有爱心的，直到事情不如他们所愿时，他们就可能变得很难相处。今天的教会是不是用这样的方式向世人显出爱？只要一切顺利，没有人踩到我们的脚趾，我们都相处融洽、彼此相爱。然而一旦有了值得争论的事，我们就戴上“拳击手套”。圣经不是说“爱是恒久忍耐，又有恩慈；爱是不嫉妒，不自夸，不张狂……凡事包容，凡事相信，凡事盼望，凡事忍耐”（林前13:4,7）吗？在面对逆境或弟兄得罪我们时，真爱便显明出来。那种爱会向世人表明我们是耶稣的门徒。

我们是否足够爱我们的弟兄以在他有需要时帮助他？也许他在某方面不自觉地远离神。我们爱他有多深？有人认为爱只是谈论彼此之间的积极事，但若我们真心爱弟兄，我们就会存着爱去找他，诚实地与他说话。若我们施行舍己并顺服弟兄的生活方式，这事应当顺利发生。倘若有弟兄来指出我们的错误，我们却发怒，那可要不得。

当我们选择与神的子民一同受苦并彼此舍己时，我们就会欣赏当弟兄姊妹把话说到我们生命里的时候。我们不会轻易被冒犯。

为彼此受苦，并为彼此舍己，常常形成彼此坚定的爱。这种爱是我们周围的世人所不认识但极为渴望的。随着日子流逝，世人愈发自私与独立。我们不能错过向他们展示神的能力与我们彼此相爱的机会。

历代敬虔之人在他们的时代有机会服侍王并传播神国的信息，但他们已离开而进入永恒。今天轮到我们了。庄稼已经熟成，可以收割。让我们投入其中，并在神的帮助下，为我们的子孙、下一代保守耶稣基督这荣耀的教会。

What do we think about when we think of the term ‘church’? We live in a day when there are many and varied churches. If one church doesn’t suit you, there are others to choose from. While some churches encourage their people to live for God and others instead of themselves, other churches promote a gospel that says lots of money and a better life now are the results of following Christ. However, there are still churches that try to follow what the Bible says—Sola scriptura (scripture alone). Traditionally, the conservative Anabaptist churches in America have tried to function in this manner. But is that changing?

We live in a day when lines are being crossed, blurred, and confused. People aren’t sure what is true and what is not. Today, men and women around the world are looking for answers and solutions, but where should they look?

I was talking with a young man who testified of being converted at a young age. He attended church faithfully and was considered quite gifted. But there was a problem—he had a sin that he still could not control. As he wrestled with God and pled for victory, he began to hear a recurring message from other professing Christians, “No one is perfect!” “We all have issues.” “Everyone has sinned!” Finally, this young man accepted his sin as normal. He justified it because it seemed that everyone was saying they had sin also, that they were not living in complete victory. It led this young man to a place of complete ruin.

Are we preaching and accepting a defeated Gospel—a gospel that doesn’t offer complete forgiveness and complete victory? Many youth of today are confused. Many people in today’s world don’t understand. Anyone can go to church and try to be a better person. But what about the all-powerful, life-changing gospel of Jesus Christ?

The apostle Paul says that Jesus is coming back for “. . .a glorious church, not having spot, or wrinkle, or any such thing; but that it should be holy and without blemish” (Eph. 5:27). And Jesus Himself said “. . .That thou art Peter, and upon this rock I will build my church; and the gates of hell shall not prevail against it” (Matt. 16:18).

Before I was converted, I was certainly a slave to sin, but I wanted victory. I was addicted to drugs and alcohol, but I didn’t like it. I wanted to be free. I went to counseling and rehab facilities all over America, but it didn’t work. I had no power. I could quit for a few days or even weeks, then anger and depression would set in, and I would return to the substances. One day, I came face to face with the Creator. The hand of the almighty God got ahold of me and opened my eyes. I repented of my sins and was given a clean slate and a clean heart. I never went back. Drugs, alcohol, and two packs of cigarettes a day were finished—forever.

I could hardly believe what God was doing. The power of God was real. I could not overcome it by myself, as none of us can, but God has promised us freedom from bondage and a new life of victorious living if we submit our lives to him. This ability to overcome the power of sin and then walk in victory is what the world is looking for. Do we believe that God can free us not only from substance abuse but also from anger, selfishness, bitterness, greed, and pride? God’s Word says “If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins, and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness” (1 John 1:9). No one is interested in a defeated Gospel, no one except those who are living in defeat because they have chosen the things of this world over God and His Word.

Are we willing to testify of the power of the resurrection? We need to proclaim a gospel that completely saves people from the bondage of sin—forever. We must be bold and confident in our faith so we can lead people to the Master.

I was witnessing to a man when he said in a rather loud voice, “God is not real!” My six-year-old son’s mouth fell open, and he gasped, “Daddy, he just told a lie!”

My son doesn’t need to be convinced that God is real; he believes it with all his heart. The world out there does need to be convinced. They need to see something that science cannot explain. They need to see something that defies all odds.

That something is a heart that has been truly changed. The fighter now loves his enemies. The person with an anger problem now loves others unconditionally. Broken families are healed. Wretched sinners are forgiven and living a transformed life. Hope, peace, love, and power are freely given to men and women who seemingly have no hope. “The blind receive their sight, and the lame walk, the lepers are cleansed, and the deaf hear, the dead are raised up, and the poor have the gospel preached to them ” (Matt. 11:5).

Are you living your life so the world can see the work of God being practical, effective, and real every day? Here are a few things the Church needs in our day to once again draw in the lost.

A willingness to suffer

History would show that the church, all through the ages, has suffered for Christ. It was part of the cost of following Christ. The Bible says, “Yea, and all that will live godly in Christ Jesus shall suffer persecution” (2 Tim. 3:12). It was something that just happened.

Today, many people want the American dream. Folks live a good moral life, are good citizens, make a good living, and go to church on Sundays. But is that what we are called to? The gospel spread like wildfire when the church suffered persecution and did so willingly and joyfully. It was something the world had never seen—a faith that people showed by their life, and their death was something worth dying for. Let’s not be afraid to suffer for Christ today.

Denial of self

Then said Jesus unto his disciples, “If any man will come after me, let him deny himself, and take up his cross, and follow me” (Matt. 16:24).

Have you ever wondered why Jesus instructs us to deny ourselves? After all, He gave us desires and passions, so why must we deny them? I have heard people say that we need to align our will with God’s, but I do not find this in the Bible. Rather, we should simply deny our will and accept God’s will.

I remember the first day of boot camp when I joined the Marine Corps after graduating from high school. Close to one hundred young men were there. We all had our own desires and thoughts. We had our own identity. It was amazing to see all the diversity. It would have been a disaster if the United States of America had sent us off to battle that first day. So, they had a plan set in place to fix this problem. Over the next three months, they broke us. Physically and mentally, we learned how to deny ourselves and submit to our commanders and each other. The world is often amazed by the great discipline and unity for which the Marines are known.

When we become a part of the kingdom of God, we cannot be effective if we each do what we want. A body of believers can all have good intentions, but if any one person has not denied themselves, they will never be able to submit to the greater cause. There is a war raging, and we cannot fight it alone. We must deny ourselves, join forces with our brethren, and fight for victory in our homes, churches, and lives.

Submission

The Bible calls us to submit ourselves:

  • to God (Jas. 4:7).
  • [to those] that have the [spiritual] rule over you [us] (Heb. 13:17).
  • to every ordinance of man for the Lord’s sake (1 Pet. 2:13).
  • one to another in the fear of God (Eph. 5:21).

Once we deny ourselves, then and only then, can we submit to others. Many people today have great difficulty in submitting to their fellow man. Some feel they are free in Christ; therefore, they can do as they please. There is a reason why we are instructed to submit to others. It is easy for us to drift away from sound doctrine when we believe we can figure everything out on our own.

When we have truly denied ourselves, we find that it is rather easy, and even a great blessing, to submit to the brotherhood. In fact, it is true freedom. What you want doesn’t matter, and you begin to depend on your brothers and sisters. When getting our own way isn’t important to us, then when we don’t get our way, we are fine with it. As we lay down our lives for each other, we become a force that the world doesn’t understand. The world was drawn to the church for centuries, wanting what it had. But amazingly, today, it seems the church is being drawn to the world, wanting what it has.

There is power in submission. Hundreds of years ago, a man named Alexander the Great conquered almost all of the then-known world using military strength and cleverness mixed with diplomacy.

The story is told that Alexander and a small company of soldiers approached a strongly fortified, walled city. Standing outside the walls, Alexander raised his voice and demanded to see the king. When the king arrived, Alexander insisted that the king surrender the city and its inhabitants to Alexander and his little band of fighting men.

The king laughed, “Why should I surrender to you? You can’t do us any harm!” So, Alexander offered to give the king a demonstration. He ordered his men to line up single file and start marching. He marched them straight toward a sheer cliff.

The townspeople gathered on the wall and watched in shocked silence as, one by one, Alexander’s soldiers marched, without hesitation, right off the cliff to their deaths! After ten soldiers died, Alexander ordered the rest of the men to return to his side. The townspeople and the king immediately surrendered to Alexander the Great. They realized that if a few men were actually willing to commit suicide at the command of this dynamic leader, then nothing could stop his eventual victory.

Obedience

Submission and obedience go hand in hand. If we are willing to submit to something or someone, we will want to obey it. It becomes very important to submit to those who are over us, especially the almighty God in Heaven. If we struggle to submit, we will usually struggle with obedience. God forbid if we begin to believe that we are better off doing things alone without our brothers.

Love

“By this shall all men know that ye are my disciples, if ye have love one to another” (John 13:35).

People wave to each other at an intersection, or they will open the door for an elderly person. People are generally loving people until something doesn’t go their way. Then they can become very difficult. Is that the way the church today is showing its love to the world? As long as everything is going smoothly, and no one steps on our toes, we all get along and we love each other. Then as soon as there is something worth fighting over, we put the “boxing gloves” on. Doesn’t the Bible say that “charity (love) beareth all things, believeth all things, hopeth all things, endureth all things” (1 Cor. 13:7)? True love is revealed when we face adversity or when a brother does something to offend us. That is the love that will show the world we are disciples of Jesus.

Do we love our brother enough to help when he is in need? Maybe he is unknowingly straying away from God in a certain area. How much do we love him? Some people think that love is only talking about positive things with each other, but if we truly love our brother, we will go to him in love and speak honestly with him. Then if we are practicing a lifestyle of denying ourselves and submitting to the brethren, it should go well. God forbid if we get angry with a brother who comes to us to show us our error.

When we have chosen to suffer with the people of God and have denied ourselves, then we appreciate when a brother or sister speaks into our lives. We will not allow ourselves to become offended.

Suffering for and with each other, plus denying ourselves for each other, often forms a solid love for one another. This type of love is the kind that the world around us does not know but desires greatly. The world is getting more selfish and independent as the days pass. We can’t afford to miss our opportunities to show them the power of God with our love for one another.

Godly people throughout the ages have had their opportunity to serve the King and spread the message of the Kingdom of God, but they have moved on to eternity. Today it is our turn. The fields are white unto harvest. Let’s plug in and, with God’s help, preserve the glorious church of Jesus Christ for our children, the next generation.
